evidence: The reviewer claimed 'bash's set -e has a known, version-dependent gap' for reply="$(drive_turn ...)"; I ran the exact shape under set -euo pipefail on bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.9 and the bare assignment aborts in both - only the local/declare form (local r=$(f)) swallows the status. The claimed failure (empty reply printed, loop continues) cannot occur at drive.sh:44, so the agent certified a non-existent bug as 'a real contract bug'.
guidance_note: Run a version-dependent shell claim in the target shell before adopting it: a bare x=$(cmd) does trip errexit; only local/declare x=$(cmd) does not.

evidence: grep -oE '^[[:alnum:] ]+' returns empty for any prompt whose first line starts with a symbol or emoji, and the guard 'if [ -n "$head" ]' then skips the paste confirmation entirely - the reviewer's read of the code is exact. The agent rejected the suggested wider-needle fallback and instead captured the pane before the paste and required it to change, which covers every prompt shape rather than widening one heuristic.
guidance_note: When a confirmation step has a branch where its needle cannot be computed, make the fallback the universal observation (the pane changed), not a looser needle.

evidence: ISO_CONFIG_DIR/ISO_WORK_DIR defaults were written independently in drive.sh, verify-driver.sh and three isolation scripts while isolation/lib.sh - sourced by all of them - owned neither; the fix moved them to lib.sh via ': ${VAR:=...}' and deleted five copies.
guidance_note: A default for a variable that a sourced lib also knows about belongs in the lib the moment the second script needs it, not copied into each caller.

evidence: The reviewer's stated mechanism is false - I tested 'T=4 f; echo $T' on bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.9 and the prefix does not persist after a function call in either - so no value leaks into a later iso_launch. The underlying complaint is still real: iso_launch read ISO_EXTRA_SETTINGS ambiently across a layer boundary, and the fix (explicit 4th positional argument) is the right shape.
guidance_note: Pass cross-layer configuration as an argument at the point the boundary is created; and when accepting a bug report, restate only the part of its mechanism you have checked.

evidence: DRV_SPINNER_SENTINEL is an env-overridable value interpolated raw into a JSON string literal ('verbs":["${DRV_SPINNER_SENTINEL}"]'), so a value containing a quote or backslash produces invalid JSON and claude silently drops --settings, leaving no working-detection token. The agent took the reject-at-the-boundary option (alphanumeric only) rather than escaping.
guidance_note: Any env-supplied value that lands inside a structured literal needs a charset gate where it enters the process, written at the same time as the interpolation.

evidence: Two independent reasons the premise fails, both checked: line 72 is outD="$(DRV_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECS=4 drive_turn ...)", a command substitution whose subshell assignments cannot reach the parent; and separately bash does not persist a function-call prefix assignment (verified on 3.2.57 and 5.3.9). Check E therefore runs with the 600s default, exactly as the agent said. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: verify-driver.sh:72 is original PR code and 39b5109 only removed that file's duplicated defaults.

narrative: Five round-0 findings, all accepted, one push in 39b5109, then a single round-1 advisory that was wrong. Three of the five accepted findings were real (paste-confirmation gap, duplicated defaults, unescaped sentinel); two rested on shell-semantics claims that do not reproduce - the errexit 'gap' (F1) and the function-prefix leak (F4). The striking pattern is that the agent accepted the function-prefix claim in round 0 and then correctly refuted the same claim in round 1 (F6) with an empirical proof, so it had the knowledge available and did not use it the first time. No finding here was caused by a fix; the round-1 finding was on original code that the fix commit merely touched.
guidance_observations: The agent's round-1 pushback (F6) is the model form: two independent reasons plus a runnable proof, and it cost one short round.
Accepting a bug report whose mechanism is a claim about the tool's semantics, without running it, put a false statement into the commit message of 39b5109.

evidence: drv_capture is 'tmux capture-pane ... 2>/dev/null' read through command substitution, so a capture failure is indistinguishable from a quiet pane: the poll loop sees empty $cur and spins to a generic timeout. The agent did not add the suggested exit-code check to drv_capture; it branched on the empty capture in drive_turn and re-checked has-session there to name the cause, which also closes the TOCTOU the reviewer raised.
guidance_note: When a helper swallows stderr and the caller reads only its stdout, decide at write time what an empty result means and branch on it rather than letting it fall into the timeout path.

evidence: README line 35 said 'all five checks' while the table it introduces listed six rows after the PR added check F - real drift, introduced by this PR's own first commit. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: 835d144 touched only evals/driver/lib.sh, so the drift predates the F1 fix. The fix was itself incomplete - I read README at b2e762e and line 77 still reads '- verify-driver.sh - the five live checks above', and the PR merged in that state.
guidance_note: When a change adds a row to a table, update every count of that table in the same commit; and when correcting a count, grep the file for the old number instead of editing the line you were pointed at.

evidence: Switching drv_capture to '-S -' widened the string fed to drv_frame_working/drv_frame_idle from the visible pane to the whole scrollback, and the code's own comment asserted - without any guard - that the TUI never scrolls its footer into history; a single stale 'esc to interrupt' anywhere in history would hang every turn. The agent added drv_live_frame (last ISO_PANE_HEIGHT lines) and classified on that, which is the reviewer's suggestion. Flag is a false positive for causation: the '-S -' capture is this PR's original commit, not the F1 fix.
guidance_note: When you widen the input to an existing classifier, re-slice the input for that classifier in the same change instead of documenting an assumption about why the wider input is still safe.

evidence: I ran the pattern: case with *"row 1"*BIGDONE-9Z* matches both 'row 1 ... BIGDONE-9Z' and '"row 1" ... BIGDONE-9Z' on bash 5.3.9. The double quotes are shell quoting around a glob segment, not characters to match, so the reviewer's two 'alternatives' are byte-identical to the existing pattern after parsing.

narrative: Three rounds over a 70-line change. Round 0's finding was real and got a better fix than the one proposed; round 1 found one genuine fragility (scrollback-wide classification) and one doc-count drift, both from this PR's own first commit rather than from the round-0 fix; round 2 produced a single finding that was a misreading of bash case quoting, correctly refuted. No finding in the packet was caused by an earlier fix, so no round here was avoidable by better fixing - but the F2 fix was incomplete and merged that way (README line 77 still says 'five live checks'), which the round-2 summary noticed and no one actioned.
guidance_observations: Two of the three rounds existed to deliver one advisory finding each; the reviewer surfaces one issue per round from code it had already read, which is the main round-count driver on this PR.

A round-2 summary observation ('the fix on line 35 didn't reach that later mention') was never turned into a thread and merged unfixed - review-summary prose outside a thread gets no reply and no action.

evidence: The coupling to 'Claude Max' and to the left column of the banner is real, but the ticket's whole point was to read the model from state rather than quiz the model, and there is no stable TUI contract to depend on instead - so the reviewer's proposed 'documented contract' does not exist to be used, and its failure mode is a loud FAIL, never a false pass. The agent took only the half that is buildable: lift the anchor into ISO_PLAN_TOKEN with a comment recording the coupling as deliberate.
guidance_note: When a check must read another tool's UI text, name the anchor as one documented overridable constant at the point it is introduced, and record in the comment that the coupling is deliberate and fails safe.

narrative: One advisory finding on a refactor that replaced model-quizzing with banner-reading, and a clean second round. The agent split the finding correctly: it accepted the maintainability half (make the anchor a named override) and declined the half that would have required a TUI contract that does not exist, saying so explicitly rather than silently doing less. One round of cost for one real improvement.
guidance_observations: The 'partly accept' reply names which half is being declined and why, which is what let the second round approve without re-litigating.

evidence: Same claim as laws#1/F1 and it fails the same test: out="$(task_validate "$1")" is a bare top-level assignment under set -euo pipefail, and on bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.9 a failing command substitution there aborts the script - VALID is never printed. The gap the reviewer names exists only for the local/declare form. The agent adopted it a second time and called it 'same class as the drive.sh finding', turning an unchecked claim into a precedent.
guidance_note: Before reusing a previous round's reasoning as precedent, re-run the one command that would falsify it; a wrong shell fact repeated across PRs is cheaper to kill on first sight.

evidence: README lines 62-64 promised '1 = criterion failed, any other nonzero = harness error' while task_die exited 1 and both check.sh files exited 1 for missing tools, so no consumer could tell a verdict from a broken harness - the doc and the code genuinely disagreed. The agent chose the reviewer's second option (deliver the fine-grained contract) over the first (weaken the doc), which is right for a harness whose stated purpose is never to fabricate a verdict.
guidance_note: Deciding to change what an exit code means is a sweep, not an edit: list every producer and consumer of the code before touching the first one.

evidence: check-task.sh's header comment promised 'any other nonzero (via task_die) = the harness could not run' while task_die exited 1 - the comment described a distinction the code did not make. Confirmed in c3ecc1a's diff, which changes task_die from exit 1 to exit 2. Same underlying defect as F2, reported against the comment instead of the README.

'Add set -e for consistency' is wrong for this script - verify-tasks.sh must accumulate failures and keep going, as the sibling verify-driver.sh does - but the concrete hazard the reviewer used to argue it (a failing find yielding a short task list read as success) was real. The agent declined -e with a stated reason, added a comment recording why, and hardened discovery with an explicit exit check instead.
guidance_note: Answer the hazard a style finding is built on, not the style rule: when declining a blanket flag, close the specific hole it was invoked for and say in the code why the flag is absent.

evidence: Missing pnpm and a failed install both exited 1, the code the README reserved for a genuine suite failure, so verify-tasks.sh would report 'criterion should PASS on the clean pinned state but did not' when the real cause was an absent tool. c3ecc1a moves both guards to exit 2.
guidance_note: An infra guard and a verdict must not share an exit code; give the guard its own code the moment you write it.

evidence: '[ -d evals ] || exit 1' made a missing checkout tree indistinguishable from a failing criterion, and task_check collapsed all nonzero to FAIL, so a broken checkout produced a fabricated verdict - exactly the outcome the file's own header says it prevents. Fixed to exit 2 with task_check aborting on >=2.

c3ecc1a changed task_die to exit 2 but left 'out="$(task_validate "$dir")" || exit 1' in task_prepare (I read the commit: lib.sh's patch touches only task_die and task_check), so the new harness-error code was rewritten to a FAIL verdict at the one call site the fix did not visit. The same reviewer had cited that exact line in round 0 as the correct idiom to copy, which is how it survived the sweep.
guidance_note: When a fix changes the meaning of an error code, grep the tree for every 'exit', '|| exit' and case on that code before pushing - the call sites are the fix, not the definition.

evidence: c3ecc1a rewrote the README's Exit-code contract section but left the Environment paragraph saying a missing tool 'exits nonzero (a conservative FAIL)', directly contradicting the check.sh files the same commit changed to exit 2. Confirmed by reading both c3ecc1a and 0715133, which fixes only that one sentence.
guidance_note: After rewriting a contract section in a doc, grep the whole doc for the old vocabulary ('conservative FAIL', 'nonzero') rather than editing the section the finding pointed at.

evidence: The F4 fix replaced 'mapfile -t TASKS < <(find ... -exec dirname {} \;)' with 'found=$(find ...)' plus 'printf %s\\n "$found" | ...', and printf of an empty string emits one blank line - so zero tasks became one empty TASKS element that passed the '-gt 0' guard, where the old process-substitution form produced zero elements. The hardening introduced the phantom entry it was later patched for.
guidance_note: When you replace a stream with a captured variable, re-derive the empty case before pushing: an empty capture becomes one blank line under printf and one blank element under mapfile.

evidence: c3ecc1a moved both check.sh files' infra guards to exit 2 and left both setup.sh files exiting 1 for the same class of failure (missing source file, regression did not apply); 0715133 then changes exactly those four lines. The agent's own round-0 plan said it would deliver the contract 'end to end', so the sibling scripts were in scope and were not swept.
guidance_note: A contract change applies to every script in the format, not the file the finding named - sweep sibling scripts with the same guard shape in the same commit.

evidence: 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile >/dev/null 2>&1' discards the only diagnostic a failed install produces while the file header claims no-silent-failure. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: I read c3ecc1a and it changed only that line's exit code from 1 to 2; the 2>&1 is original PR code.
guidance_note: Silence a tool's chatter with >/dev/null alone; 2>&1 throws away the channel you will need when the guard fires.

evidence: git clone/checkout ran with 2>/dev/null, so 'git clone failed: $repo' was the entire diagnosis for an auth, network or disk failure. Flag is a false positive for causation: 0715133 (the named fix commit) touches task_prepare's '|| exit $?' only - I read its patch - and the suppression is original PR code.
guidance_note: When a finding names one silenced diagnostic, sweep every 2>/dev/null in the changed files in that same fix - the reviewer will otherwise return with the rest one round at a time.

evidence: '. "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1' hid the shell's own syntax-error message behind 'manifest.sh failed to source cleanly', leaving the maintainer to re-run by hand. Original PR code, untouched by the named fix commit 0715133 - the flag is a false positive for causation.

A process substitution's exit status is unreachable in bash, so 'while read ... done < <(find evals ...)' turns a find that dies mid-traversal into zero iterations, failed=0 and exit 0 - a fabricated PASS from a criterion whose stated contract forbids exactly that. Original PR code; 0715133 did not touch this file, so the flag is a false positive for causation.
guidance_note: Enumerate into a checked capture, never a process substitution, whenever the enumeration's failure would read as an empty result.

evidence: 'bash -n "$script" 2>/dev/null' discarded the line and token of the syntax error the criterion exists to detect, leaving only the filename. Original PR code, untouched by 0715133 - the flag is a false positive for causation.

'( cd "$state" && exec "$abs/check.sh" )' returns 1 when cd fails, and c3ecc1a's new case statement maps 1 to 'criterion FAIL' - so the fine-grained contract the fix introduced is violated by the very function the fix rewrote (I read both c3ecc1a and c350084, which adds 'cd "$state" || exit 2'). Before that fix every nonzero was a FAIL, so this finding only became expressible because of the contract change.
guidance_note: When you introduce a code that means 'not a verdict', audit every path inside the verdict function that can produce 1 without running the thing being judged.

evidence: Zero .sh files under evals/ left failed=0 and exit 0 - a vacuous PASS - and the enumeration it lives in had just been rewritten by the F14 fix in 3c77022 without an emptiness guard, one round after the identical empty-collection gap was fixed in verify-tasks.sh (F9). c350084 adds '[ -n "$scripts" ] || exit 2'.
guidance_note: Fixing an empty-collection gap in one enumerator is a signal to check every other enumerator in the same change for the same gap.

evidence: '[ ! -e "$dir/setup.sh" ] || [ -x "$dir/setup.sh" ]' admits a directory named setup.sh (both -e and -x are true for a directory) while the sibling line validates check.sh with -f, and task_setup then exec's it. The reply-hint says pushback but the only reply is 'Fixed in 7a7bbee' - the agent accepted. Flag is a false positive for causation: c350084 touched check.sh and task_check, not this line, which is original PR code.
guidance_note: Validate an existence predicate for the operation that follows it: a path you will exec must be checked as a regular file, and neighbouring checks on sibling files must use the same test.

narrative: Five rounds, eighteen findings, and the only PR in this batch with real fix-caused findings. Round 0's F2/F3 turned a loose exit-code contract into a fine-grained 0/1/2 one, and that decision - correct in itself - was implemented file by file rather than swept, so rounds 1-3 kept returning call sites the contract change had invalidated (F7 task_prepare, F10 both setup.sh, F16 task_check's cd path) plus one doc paragraph it had contradicted (F8). Separately, the F4 discovery hardening introduced the phantom-empty-task bug the reviewer found next round (F9). The other eight findings were pre-existing issues in original code that the reviewer surfaced one class per round - silenced stderr in round 1 (F11) then four more instances of it in round 2 (F12-F15) - so a class sweep at the first instance would have removed a whole round.
guidance_observations: A mid-review contract change is the highest-cost move in this batch: three later findings and part of a fourth round exist only because the new meaning of exit 1 was applied where the finding pointed rather than everywhere the code produces it.
The reviewer reports one instance of a class per round; the agent fixed one instance per round in reply, and the two behaviours multiplied into five rounds.
The last round's reply skipped the plan step entirely ('Fixed in 7a7bbee') and the PR merged 23 seconds later, so the final change went in with no stated reasoning and no re-review.

evidence: f="$(cfg_fields "$cfg")" discards the exit status, and an empty $f makes $skill empty, which is precisely the control-arm signal the next branch tests - so a failed read is reported as a passing control arm. The agent guarded cfg_fields with '|| { fail; continue; }' and wrapped cfg_resolve in an if that reports its stderr.
guidance_note: In a verifier, every value that feeds a pass/fail branch needs its producer's exit status checked at the point of capture - an empty string that happens to be a legal input is the worst kind of silent failure.

evidence: cfg_body_path interpolated $skill straight into skills/$skill/references/craft.md with no charset check, so CONFIG_SKILL='../foo' resolves outside skills/ at the ref; low practical risk with checked-in manifests but it breaks the name-to-directory invariant the resolver rests on. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: ad08356 changed only evals/configs/verify-configs.sh (I listed its files), and cfg_body_path is original code.
guidance_note: A manifest field that becomes a path component gets a token charset gate where it is parsed, in the same commit that first uses it as a path.

evidence: The duplication is real, but it was deliberate oracle independence: expected_body is the verifier's own answer, and having it call cfg_body_path makes the test agree with the implementation by construction, which the reviewer's fix does not acknowledge. The agent took the fix and restored the lost independence by adding two literal assertions (code -> skills/code/SKILL.md, prompt -> skills/prompt/references/craft.md), so the derivation still has an external oracle. Flag is a false positive for causation: the duplication is original code in a file the fix commit happened to touch.
guidance_note: When a verifier deliberately re-derives what it checks, say so in the comment - unexplained duplication in test code reads as drift risk and buys a round.

narrative: Three rounds, three findings, all accepted, none caused by a fix - the two round-1 findings were pre-existing issues in code the round-0 fix commit merely sat next to. The round-0 finding was the sharpest of the batch: an unchecked command substitution whose empty result is a legal value (the control arm), producing a false PASS. The F3 exchange is the one place a reviewer's DRY finding cut against a deliberate property (an independent oracle in the verifier) and the agent kept both by adding literal assertions rather than arguing.
guidance_observations: Two of three rounds delivered findings on code the reviewer had already reviewed once; nothing the agent did differently would have removed them.
The agent's habit of adding an independent assertion when told to deduplicate a verifier is worth keeping - it is the answer to a DRY finding that would otherwise weaken a test.

evidence: The same two footer literals ('? for shortcuts', 'bypass permissions on') decided idle-ness in iso_is_idle_frame and drv_frame_idle, and this diff added the new bypass token to both copies rather than to one owner - drift would break launch-settle or turn-completion silently. The agent extracted iso_has_idle_footer in the isolation layer and had both classifiers read it.
guidance_note: When a diff adds the same literal to two functions in two layers, that is the moment to extract the owner, not after the reviewer counts the copies.

evidence: The bytes produced by a command substitution are not re-scanned for quoting, word splitting or further substitution, so quotes, backticks and $() inside the skill body are inert data inside "$(cat file)"; the agent also cited a live run that loaded the 57KB laws:code body through this exact path. The reviewer's 'shell word-splitting inside double quotes' and its command-injection escalation are both false.

'tmux send-keys "2"; sleep 1; tmux send-keys C-m' sequences a menu selection on elapsed time against a dialog whose default is 'No, exit', so a slow frame makes the Enter quit the session - and the same file's own settle loop already polls for observed state instead. The agent replaced the sleep with a gate on the observed 'Yes, I accept' selection.
guidance_note: Sequence a keystroke against the screen state it depends on, not a sleep, especially where the wrong ordering selects a destructive default.

evidence: The driver-side half of F1 - same duplicated footer literals, reported against drv_frame_idle - and fixed by the same extraction of iso_has_idle_footer.

The hazard is the same one F3 names and is real, but the suggested remedy (use $ISO_POLL_SECS instead of 1, or name the constant) only relabels the timing bet - a longer sleep is still a sleep against a dialog that defaults to exit. The agent removed the sleep entirely in favour of the state gate, which answers both findings.
guidance_note: A finding that proposes tuning a magic timeout is usually evidence the timing dependency itself should go.

evidence: run_emit_outcome interpolated $artifact, $transcript and two basenames into a JSON here-doc, and $artifact derives from the CLI's out-dir argument, so a quote or backslash in a path emits a malformed record - the comment above it asserting 'values are shell strings with no embedded quotes' was simply untrue for CLI-supplied values. The agent replaced the writer with python3 json.dumps.
guidance_note: A comment claiming a value cannot contain a delimiter is a claim about every caller; if the value arrives from a CLI argument, encode instead of asserting.

evidence: iso_launch validates sysprompt_file with [ -f ] on the host but embeds it in a command string that runs after 'cd "$wd"' in the session shell, and $(cat missing) yields empty with no error inside a command substitution - so a relative path silently launches the arm with no skill body, which would score as a real verdict. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: the --append-system-prompt "$(cat %q)" line is original PR code (it is the subject of round-0 finding F2), and 0a97783 changed the idle tokens, the bypass handler and the JSON writer.
guidance_note: Canonicalize a path to absolute at the boundary where you validate it whenever the consumer runs after a cd - validation and use must resolve against the same directory.

narrative: Six round-0 findings on the largest change in the batch, five accepted and one refuted, then one round-1 finding on original code and a clean round 2. The refutation (F2, the claim that file content inside "$(cat ...)" is re-scanned by the shell) was correct and well argued, and the two timing findings (F3, F5) were answered by deleting the timing dependency rather than tuning it. Nothing here was caused by a fix: the round-1 finding names the same line round 0 had already reviewed, from the other end (relative-path resolution rather than quoting).
guidance_observations: The two silent-guidance-loss risks in this PR - a malformed outcome record and an empty --append-system-prompt - both fail by producing a scored verdict from a run that did not have what it claimed; a verifier that asserts the loaded body is non-empty would have caught the class before review.
Five findings of six were answered in one round with one commit, which is the cheap shape: the cost driver on this PR was breadth of the original change, not fix quality.

evidence: $out/$name.runlog and $out/$name are keyed on basename, so two config dirs with the same basename (a real possibility once arms live in different trees) silently overwrite the first arm's runlog and out dir, losing a run record in a tool whose product is run records. The agent chose the loud refusal over the disambiguated names, which is right for a comparison that must not quietly report on the wrong artifact.
guidance_note: When a loop derives a filesystem key from an input, check the keys are distinct before the loop rather than discovering the collision as an overwrite.

evidence: The verdict-to-rank mapping (pass 2, fail 1, else 0) was written twice inside cmp_report, once to compute the best rank and once to pick the winners; divergence would name a winner that is not the best row. Extracted to cmp_rank, which laws#8 then reused.
guidance_note: Two loops over the same array that both classify its elements want one classifier function from the start.

narrative: Two advisory findings in one round, both real, both accepted with the right variant of the fix, and a clean second round - the cheapest PR in the batch. Neither finding was caused by a fix. The cmp_rank extraction here is what made laws#8's reviewer able to say 'cmp_rank has a default case and this does not', so the fix paid off one PR later.
guidance_observations: Both findings are shapes an author can self-check before pushing: a filesystem key derived from an input, and the same case statement written twice in one function.

evidence: compare_repeated is compare_task adapted for N repetitions and it dropped the '[ -n "$verdict" ] || verdict=FAILED' line the original has right after the same grep+sed - an empty verdict then matches neither case arm, so the repetition disappears from both counters and k-of-N silently shrinks. The reviewer's line-by-line comparison against the sibling is exact.
guidance_note: When adapting an existing function into a variant, diff the two side by side before pushing and account for every guard the original had.

evidence: The verdict dispatch matched only 'pass' and 'FAILED', so 'fail' - the verdict run_emit_outcome actually produces most often - fell through both counters, while the neighbouring cmp_rank already had a total mapping. The agent made the case total: pass, explicit fail, and a default that counts as aborted.
guidance_note: A case statement over a value another function produces must enumerate that function's full output set and end in a default; the sibling that already does so is the spec.

evidence: The reviewer's mechanism is wrong - I ran it: [ "08" -ge 1 ] is true on bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.9, the [ builtin parses base 10 and emits no error - but the hazard is real one line later, where 'for ((i=1; i<=reps; i++))' and 'printf %02d 08' both fail with 'value too great for base' because arithmetic context reads 08 as octal. Accepting was the right call for a reason the thread never states. Flag is a false positive for causation: the reps validation is original PR code (it appears in round-0 finding F2's hunk) and ba7a8aa restored the verdict guard and the default case.
guidance_note: Validate a numeric input into the form its consumer needs - decimal, no leading zero - at the parse boundary, because bash arithmetic and printf %d read a leading zero as octal.

narrative: Two round-0 findings, both from comparing the new compare_repeated against the compare_task it was adapted from, and both real: a dropped guard and a non-total case statement. The round-1 finding was on original code, not on the fix, and its stated mechanism was wrong even though its conclusion was right. The pattern worth carrying out of this PR is that every finding here was findable by diffing the new function against the older one it was cloned from.
guidance_observations: All three findings are copy-adaptation defects; a self-review that diffs a new variant against its source function would have caught two of three before the first round.
The agent accepted a finding whose stated mechanism is false and never checked it - the fix was right by luck, and the thread now records an incorrect claim about bash's [ builtin.
